TE-CS-0022: Extended investigation of synthetic data exfiltration indicator on TE-AS-03. The case spanned several shifts because the affected service owner could only be reached after the weekend change window. Analysts rebuilt the event timeline from endpoint, directory and gateway records, compared it with the approved change calendar, and found that two of the three suspicious sequences were caused by an unapproved but benign configuration rollout. The remaining sequence was traced to a misconfigured service account whose permissions were wider than its documented role; the account was rotated, the permissions were reduced, and the access change was reviewed by the system owner. A supervisor reviewed the timeline, the containment steps and the evidence package before approving closure, and the recovery test was repeated after the credential rotation to confirm that the dependent service behaved normally. Residual risk was recorded in the synthetic risk register, detection logic was tuned to reduce repeat noise, and a follow-up review was scheduled for the next monthly cycle. Referenced identifier SYN-CVE-2026-2985 is fictional and is not a real CVE.
Auto-closed: approved SYN-AUTO rule
